attributes.description: Alerts when the HTTP 5xx error rate in a single Vercel execution region exceeds 5% over a 15-minute window, even if the global error rate looks healthy. A regional error concentration typically indicates edge/lambda infrastructure issues localized to that region rather than a global code defect.
attributes.name: [Vercel OTel] Regional error rate skew

investigation_guide.blob:
## Regional Error Rate Skew

### Triage Steps
1. Note the affected `vercel.execution.region` from the alert context (e.g. `iad1`, `sfo1`, `pdx1`).
2. Compare against the global error rate rule — if this rule fires alone (global rate is healthy), the issue is localized to the region's edge/lambda infrastructure rather than a code-level regression.
3. Inspect recent errors scoped to the region: `FROM logs-vercel.logs.otel-default | WHERE vercel.execution.region == "<region>" AND http.response.status_code >= 500 | KEEP @timestamp, http.route, message, deployment.id | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 50`
4. Check the Vercel status page for any reported incidents affecting that region.
5. If this is a regional infra issue outside your control, there is typically no remediation available beyond monitoring; if it is caused by a downstream dependency only reachable from that region (e.g. a database replica), investigate that dependency's health in the affected region.

### Escalation
If the regional skew persists for more than 30 minutes or if the region also shows in the traffic-skew visualisation, escalate to the on-call engineer and consider filing a report with Vercel support.

esqlQuery.esql:
FROM logs-vercel.logs.otel-default
| WHERE deployment.environment.name == "production"
    AND vercel.log.source IN ("lambda", "edge")
    // -1 means the function crashed before returning any response; excluded here
    AND http.response.status_code != -1
| STATS
    total = COUNT(*),
    errors = COUNT(*) WHERE http.response.status_code >= 500
  BY vercel.execution.region
// Minimum sample size per region to avoid noisy alerts on low-traffic regions
| WHERE total > 20
| EVAL region_error_rate_pct = ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(errors) / total * 100.0, 2)
// Regional threshold is set higher than the global 5xx rule (2%) because a single region naturally has
// higher variance with a smaller sample; adjust based on your regional traffic distribution.
| WHERE region_error_rate_pct > 5.0
| SORT region_error_rate_pct DESC
| LIMIT 10
